config.title: 3Sum

intro.title: 3Sum
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that solves the 3Sum lesson: finding all unique triplets in an array that add up to zero. You will learn the core concept of using a two-pointer technique to efficiently search for combinations without checking every possible set. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, loops, and conditional logic. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to a common algorithmic pattern used in coding interviews and real-world applications.
intro.usecase: The 3Sum algorithm solves a fundamental pattern-matching lesson that appears in many real-world applications. In e-commerce platforms, it's used to find product combinations that meet specific price targets or discount thresholds. Financial analysis tools apply it to identify investment trios that sum to target returns or risk levels. Data dashboards use similar logic to filter datasets where three metrics combine to reach critical thresholds, helping analysts spot trends and correlations.

objectives: Implement a brute-force solution to find all unique triplets that sum to zero
Apply sorting to optimize the 3Sum algorithm by reducing time complexity
Construct a two-pointer technique to efficiently search for complementary pairs
Manipulate arrays to skip duplicate values and ensure unique triplets
Initialize and update pointers to traverse the sorted array during pair searches
Integrate edge case handling for arrays with fewer than three elements
Control loop structures to iterate through each element as a potential first value

content.body: Welcome! Today we'll solve the 3Sum lesson. You'll learn how to find three numbers in an array that add up to zero. This builds on the 'remember what we've seen' approach from Two Sum.
content.title: Introduction

content.body:
1. Apply the 'remember what we've seen' mental model to three numbers.
2. Implement a solution using sorting and a hash map.
3. Explain why we sort first and how the hash map avoids duplicate triplets.
4. Identify when to check the hash map versus add to it.
content.title: What you'll learn
Try it
content.prompt: Find three numbers that add to 0.

content.title: Try a bigger array
content.prompt: Find three numbers that add to 0.
content.successMessage: Well done! You might have found [-2, 0, 2] or [-1, 0, 1].

content.title: One more
content.prompt: Find three numbers that add to 0.
content.successMessage: Excellent! You checked many triplets, like [-2, -1, 3] or [-4, 1, 3].

content.body: You just did a brute force search: checking all combinations of three numbers. That works for small arrays but becomes very slow for larger ones.
content.title: What you did

content.body: With 1,000 numbers, checking every triplet is impractical. We need a smarter method. Can't figure it out? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Remember what we have already seen. We'll use a lookup structure (like a Set or Map) to remember values we've encountered, avoiding repeated scans. For 3Sum, we fix one number and then solve a Two Sum lesson for the remaining two.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Think of a notebook where we write down numbers we've seen. For each fixed number, we check if the needed complement is already in our notebook.

content.body: We'll sort the array first to easily skip duplicates. Then, for each number, we'll treat the rest as a Two Sum lesson using a hash set.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Array: [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]
Sorted: [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]
Fix -2 → need two numbers that sum to 2. Use set: check -1 (need 3? not in set), add -1; check 0 (need 2? not in set), add 0; check 1 (need 1? not in set), add 1; check 2 (need 0? yes, in set). Found [-2, 0, 2]. Move to next fixed number.

content.body:
1. Sort the array.
2. Loop through each number as the fixed first element.
3. Skip duplicates for the fixed element.
4. Use a set to find two numbers in the remaining array that sum to -fixed.
5. Skip duplicates within the Two Sum search.
6. Collect valid triplets.
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Sort the array
steps.instruction: Start by sorting the input array. This helps us skip duplicates later.
steps.hint: Use the built-in sort method. Remember to handle numeric sorting correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Good! Sorting is the first step to avoid duplicate triplets.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost. Make sure you're sorting the nums array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using nums.sort() with a compare function for numbers.

steps.title: Initialize result array
steps.instruction: Create an empty array to store the triplets we find.
steps.hint: Declare a variable and set it to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! We'll push valid triplets here.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. You need an array variable.

steps.title: Loop through fixed elements
steps.instruction: Loop through the array. Each element will be our fixed first number.
steps.hint: Use a for loop. We'll go up to nums.length - 2 because we need three numbers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! This loop will fix each number as the first element.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost. The loop should run while i < nums.length - 2.

steps.title: Skip duplicate fixed elements
steps.instruction: If the current fixed number is the same as the previous one, skip it to avoid duplicate triplets.
steps.hint: Check if i > 0 and nums[i] === nums[i - 1]. If so, use continue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. You need to check if i > 0 and nums[i] equals the previous.

steps.title: Set up Two Sum with hash set
steps.instruction: For the remaining array, use a set to find two numbers that sum to -nums[i].
steps.hint: Create a new Set. Loop from i+1 to end. Calculate complement = -nums[i] - nums[j].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost. You need a Set and an inner loop starting at i+1.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try 'const seen = new Set(); for (let j = i + 1; j < nums.length; j++)'.

steps.title: Check set and add triplets
steps.instruction: Inside the inner loop, check if the complement is in the set. If yes, add the triplet. Always add the current number to the set.
steps.hint: Calculate complement = -nums[i] - nums[j]. If set has complement, push [nums[i], complement, nums[j]]. Then add nums[j] to set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. You need to check for complement and add to the set.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try 'const complement = -nums[i] - nums[j]; if (seen.has(complement)) { result.push([nums[i], complement, nums[j]]); while (j + 1 < nums.length && nums[j] === nums[j + 1]) j++; } seen.add(nums[j]);'.

content.body: You've solved 3Sum! Remember: sort first to skip duplicates, fix one number, then use a hash set for the remaining Two Sum. The set remembers what we've seen, so we avoid re-scanning. Key decisions: store values as keys in the set, check the set before adding the current number.
content.title: Done
